title: Technical Brief — Co-Occurring Motif Experiments (Complete, Self-Contained Explanation)
summary: A rigorous experimental protocol for testing whether learning agents that compress and predict discover structured patterns (motifs) and their conditional co-occurrence relationships faster and more robustly than non-compressive agents. The document specifies a complete data-generation pipeline (HMM-based motif insertion with controlled co-occurrence statistics), five agent classes (n-gram, LZ, Bayesian HMM, LSTM/Transformer, oracle), two operational modes (passive vs. active/probing), and formal metrics (discovery time, compression gain/MDL, predictive log-likelihood, mutual information, co-occurrence matrix error). It operationalizes the core genome claim that reasoning is detectable as compressive, predictive alignment — and provides the machinery to measure it.
compress: This document converts the genome's theoretical claim that reasoning equals compressive prediction into a fully specified, falsifiable experiment with synthetic ground truth, multiple agent architectures, and formal metrics — the missing bridge between philosophy and evidence.
